sections.title: Using Orbit
sections.html:
This guide is for everyone in a household who uses Orbit day to day. It walks through the things you will want to do, in the order you are likely to meet them. For a tour of the screens themselves, see What Orbit does. For signing in, see Authentication.

The guide describes Orbit on a computer screen. On a phone the main screens have their own layout, so some controls look different.

Orbit calls a household a system. You will see both words here; they mean the same thing.

sections.title: Join or start a household
sections.html:
#Join or start a household

When you first sign in and you are not yet in a household, Orbit asks where do you belong? You have two choices.

  • Ask to join a household that already exists. Press ask to join beside its name. The row then says waiting until the household's owner approves or declines you.
  • Start your own. Press name your own system, give it a name, choose its time zone and currency, and press Create. A new household starts with four sections: Home, Vehicles, Devices and Services.

If you are already signed in but in no household, your sky says you’re adrift. Press one of the household labels in the sky to ask to join it: Orbit asks Request to join … system?, and you press request to join.

If someone invited you by email, open the link in the message. Orbit asks you to sign in, then takes you straight into that household. The link only works for someone signed in with the exact address it was sent to.

sections.title: Find your way around
sections.html:
#Find your way around

Your home screen is your sky. Each thing you look after sits on the dial, and the list below it shows the same things in date order:

  • anything overdue first, then a TODAY line;
  • then each coming month, with how many items are approaching;
  • then, under no date, anything you keep without a date.

The round button with your initials opens the menu: Inbox, Settings and About, the theme colours, ↻ watch the tour and sign out →. The inbox button opens your inbox and shows how many forwarded emails are waiting for you.

On most other screens, ← YOUR SKY takes you back home. A household screen opened from Settings shows ← SETTINGS instead.

sections.title: Add an item
sections.html:
#Add an item

  1. On your home screen, press create.
  2. The Add to your orbit drawer opens. Press renewal, service or inspection to start with that type, or something else to choose later. You can also press open the full form →.
  3. The full form opens. Type a name in Name this entry.
  4. Under type, choose one of service, renewal, inspection, suggestion or document (see the next section).
  5. Under section, choose where the item belongs. There is no default: you must choose one.
  6. Fill in whatever else you know: provider, reference / policy no., key date, recurrence, cost, reminder and notes. These fields appear once you have typed three letters of the name or chosen a type or section. A suggestion has no key date or recurrence; a document has no recurrence.
  7. Press Add to orbit. Orbit returns to your home screen with the new item open.

Press cancel to leave without saving. Once the rest of the form has opened, Orbit asks Discard this entry? before throwing it away.

You can also start from the search box: type a name that matches nothing and choose add "…" as an item.

sections.title: Choose a type
sections.html:
#Choose a type

The type decides what kind of date the item has.

Type What it is for Date Repeats
service Something done regularly, such as a boiler service optional (needed to repeat) yes
renewal Something you renew, such as insurance optional (needed to repeat) yes
inspection A check that comes round, such as an MOT optional (needed to repeat) yes
document Something that expires once, such as a passport optional no
suggestion An idea to keep, with no date no no

A document's expiry date is never counted as overdue.

sections.title: Set when it’s due
sections.html:
#Set when it’s due

  • key date is when the item is next due.
  • recurrence is how often it comes round: one-off, monthly, yearly, or every … months (1 to 120). A new item starts as yearly.

A repeating item needs a key date. If you choose a repeat without a date, Orbit will not save the item yet; either set the date or choose one-off.

Items with no date are kept at the foot of your list under no date and are not drawn on the dial.

sections.title: When Orbit says “not yet”
sections.html:
#When Orbit says “not yet”

The Add to orbit button stays unavailable until the item can be saved, and the reason is shown beside it. You may see:

  • not yet — give it a name
  • not yet — choose a section
  • not yet — choose a type
  • not yet — use a dot for pence, for example 12.50
  • not yet — a repeat needs a due date

Nothing you typed is lost while the message shows.

sections.title: Open an item
sections.html:
#Open an item

Press an item on the dial or in the list, and its drawer opens in place. It shows when the item is due, its section, type, orbital period (how often it repeats), cost, provider, reference and reminders, then its notes and documents.

Along the bottom are the things you can do: snooze, complete, attach a document and retire. At the right end, the pencil edits the item and the chain-link button copies a link to it.

sections.title: Change an item
sections.html:
#Change an item

  1. Open the item and press the pencil (edit).
  2. Change what you need. Press due, section, type or orbital period to choose from a list or calendar; type straight into cost, provider, reference, reminders and notes.
  3. Press save.

In reminders, type the number of days before the due date for each reminder you want, for example 21 7.

Press cancel to stop. If you have changed something, the button first asks discard changes?; press it again to throw the changes away.

sections.title: Mark it done
sections.html:
#Mark it done

  1. Open the item and press complete.
  2. Check completed on (it starts at today; press it to pick another day). You can also update the cost and notes.
  3. If the item repeats, Orbit shows then and the next due date.
  4. Press record.

The next due date counts from the day you say it was done, not from the old due date. An item that does not repeat, or a document, has no next date once completed; its row then says when it was done.

sections.title: Snooze it
sections.html:
#Snooze it

Press snooze in the item's drawer and choose a day from the snooze until calendar. The day must be after today. Reminders that would have arrived before that day are not sent. The due date itself does not change.

sections.text: Snooze it Press snooze in the item's drawer and choose a day from the snooze until calendar. The day must be after today. Reminders that would have arrived before that day are not sent. The due date itself does not change.

sections.title: Retire or restore an item
sections.html:
#Retire or restore an item

Press retire, then press again to confirm. The item leaves your list and the dial, but it is not deleted.

If you open a retired item again, for example from a link you copied, its drawer offers restore to bring it back.

sections.title: Find something
sections.html:
#Find something

Use the box below the dial on your home screen, explore your world. It matches item names, sections and providers, and the names of attached documents. Use the arrow keys to step through the results and Enter to open one.

sections.title: Reminders
sections.html:
#Reminders

Orbit reminds everyone in the household about each item, at 9 in the morning in the household's time zone.

  • When you add an item, the reminder field lets you pick 1 week before, 2 weeks before or 1 month before; the item then has that one reminder. If you leave it alone, the item takes your first and final warnings instead: 14 days and 3 days before. You can see them under Settings → Reminders, as first warning and final warning; they cannot be changed in the app.
  • To change an item's reminders later, edit the item and change reminders. An item can have up to 8 reminders, each up to 365 days before.
  • Completing an item ends the reminders for that date; a repeating item's reminders start again for its next date. A retired item gets none, and a snoozed item gets none before the day it is snoozed until.

#Choose how reminders reach you

Open Settings and find the Reminders card.

  • email reminders turns reminder emails on or off for you.
  • browser alerts · this device turns alerts on or off in the browser you are using now. Your browser asks for permission the first time. Turn it on in each browser where you want alerts.

Both depend on your administrator: outbound mail shows whether email is set up, and browser alerts only work if your administrator has set them up. If both switches are off, Orbit sends you nothing.

#See what was sent

The sent to you lately tab lists recent reminders: which item, which warning, and whether it went by email or browser alert. A reminder that could not be sent says so. Press one to open its item.

sections.title: Documents
sections.html:
#Documents

Orbit keeps PDFs and photos (JPEG or PNG) with your items. Each file is checked for malware before it is kept, unless your administrator has turned scanning off.

#Add a document with a new item

On the full form, drop a file on drop a document, or press it to choose one. The screen splits: the form on one side and the first page of your document on the other. Nothing is saved until you press Add to orbit; the item and the document are saved together.

If your administrator has set up document reading, Orbit reads the file and fills any empty provider, reference / policy no., key date and cost fields with what it found, each marked from document. Check each one: press ✓ accept to confirm it, or type over it.

Press not this one to take the file back out; any suggestion you have not accepted goes with it. If Orbit refuses the file, it says why, and the item cannot be added until you drop another file or press remove it to save without one.

#Attach a document to an existing item

Open the item and press attach a document, then choose the file.

#Read a document

In an item's drawer, press a document under documents. A preview of the page opens beside the drawer. Press the page to open the reader, where you can turn pages, zoom with −, + and fit, download the file, or close.

A file still being checked shows Still scanning this file until it is ready.

#Remove or restore a document

Only the person who added a document, the household's owner, or an instance administrator can remove or restore it. In the reader, press remove, then press again to confirm. Orbit keeps a removed document for a while (the preview says until when), and restore puts it back exactly as it was. After that it is gone for good.

sections.title: Forward documents by email
sections.html:
#Forward documents by email

Every member has a private relay address. Forward an email with a document attached to it, and Orbit reads it and puts it in your inbox for review. Nothing is added to your household until you say so.

This only works if your administrator has set up Orbit's mailbox.

#Set up your relay

Open Settings and press open the relay → in the Your relay card. The relay screen shows your address; click it (tap it on a phone) to copy it. If your administrator has paused ingest, the address stays and the screen says collection is paused by the administrator: mail you send now waits and is read when it resumes.

Orbit only accepts mail forwarded from the address shown as sending from. If sender check says not yet checked, press send the check email and open the link in that email within 24 hours, while signed in to Orbit. This email needs your administrator to have set up outbound mail.

On the same screen:

  • rotate address gives you a new relay address (press twice to confirm);
  • pause ingest stops Orbit collecting your forwarded mail until you press resume ingest.

#Review what arrived

Open your Inbox. Under For your review, each forwarded email shows what Orbit read from it and its attachments.

  • Add to orbit files it as an item, with its documents.
  • Dismiss throws it away.
  • review & amend → opens it on your home screen so you can correct what Orbit read, then add to orbit.

Add to orbit and Dismiss each ask you to press twice. If Orbit could not tell the item's type, it says not yet — choose a type in review & amend.

Anything left unreviewed burns up after 45 days. Items you have added are listed under Filed. Messages Orbit could not use are listed under Failed to process, with the reason.

Forwarded items also appear on your home screen as hollow circles until you decide. Open one to see the same choices.

sections.title: Your household
sections.html:
#Your household

Open your household's screen by pressing the sun in the middle of your sky, or from Settings → Your systems, which lists every household you belong to.

Everyone in a household sees its name, time zone and currency, and the Members list. Only the household's owner can change its settings or its members.

#Leave a household

In Members, press leave this system on your own row, then press again. Everything you added stays with the household.

An owner cannot leave or be removed. An owner must hand the household over first.

#For owners: add people

In Members:

  • Add someone who already has an account: press add beside them.
  • Invite by email: type their address and press send invitation. Orbit emails them a link that lasts 14 days. You can resend or withdraw it. This needs your administrator to have set up outbound mail; if not, the invitation shows not sent.
  • Knocking on the door lists people asking to join. Press approve or decline.
  • To remove someone, press remove on their row, then press again.

#For owners: hand the household over

Press hand over → on your row. Choose who takes it, then press hand over to … and press again to confirm. You stay a member and keep everything you added.

#For owners: sections

The Sections card lists the household's sections, up to 12.

  • Rename a section by typing in its name.
  • Use the switch to show or hide a section. A hidden section is not offered when adding an item.
  • Press + add a section to add one.
  • Press × to remove a section. If it still holds items, Orbit asks where they should go. You cannot remove the last section.
  • Press save to keep your changes.

#For owners: name, time zone and currency

In The system, change the name, time zone or currency and press save beside it. The time zone decides what "today" is for the household and when reminders arrive.

#For owners: take a copy of the household

The archive card writes an encrypted file of the household to download.

  1. On take it with you, press write an archive →.
  2. Choose a passphrase and type it twice. Orbit never keeps it: lose it and the file cannot be opened.
  3. Press write the archive, press again, then download the file. The file is kept for a day.

Entries and their documents go in the file; people never do. The bring one in tab merges an archive into the household. Entries that are already there stay out.

Orbit may first ask for your password, or send you to your identity provider, to confirm it is you.

#For owners: delete the household

Under The danger line, press request deletion →, type the household's name exactly, then press request deletion twice. Everything in the household stops at once. You have 30 days to change your mind: ask your administrator, who can undo it until then.

For owners: delete the household Under The danger line, press request deletion →, type the household's name exactly, then press request deletion twice. Everything in the household stops at once. You have 30 days to change your mind: ask your administrator, who can undo it until then.
